text:
alex choi: ran the headroom sims this morning, attaching quick notes. main question — should we target 70% GPU util or 85% for cost?
morgan liu: 85% buys cost but p99 jumps in the last 10% of saturation. saw p99 go from 210ms -> 430ms when util hit ~88%.
rachel nguyen: can you paste the profiling output? interested in kernel hotpaths at the tail. :eyes:
alex choi: sure, clipped the hotlines from the trace: ```
[PROFILE] microbatch=8 seq=1024 model=redwood-7b
kernel chosen: flash_attn_v2
kv-cache hit ratio: 0.72
avg latency: 92ms p95: 180ms p99: 420ms
GPU util: 88% memory 64GB/80GB
cpu spin: 6% io wait: 1.2%
```
samir patel: flash_attn_v2 looks fine but note the kernel fallback when seq>1024. we saw a fallback to slower kernel at the tail for large inputs causing that p99 spike.
praveen rao: is KV cache thrashing? 0.72 hit ratio seems low for our chat workload. if we can push hits to 0.9 we save ~25% of token latency by avoiding recompute.
alina kozlova: I ran a quick microbenchmark: varying microbatch sizes {1,4,8,16}. p95/p99 trend: microbatch=1 p95~85 p99~160, microbatch=8 p95~110 p99~320, microbatch=16 p95~140 p99~520. throughput increases with batch but tails worsen.
morgan liu: that's the classic SLO vs throughput tradeoff. For customer tier=prod-llow we should keep p99<250ms. means we either restrict microbatch<=4 or tighten admission.
ops-bot: deployment can toggle admission policy flag: admission.max_inflight_per_gpu and admission.target_util_pct
alex choi: suggested policy from sims: admission.target_util_pct=75, admission.max_inflight_per_gpu=48, microbatch_cap=8 with per-route p99 guard at 250ms. also enable kv-prefetch for hot prefixes.
rachel nguyen: simulation results for that policy? numbers please.
perf-bot: sim run results (300s synthetic mix, 60% chat short, 40% long seq): ```
policy A: util_target=75, inflight=48, microbatch_cap=8
  throughput: 92k tokens/s
  p95: 130ms p99: 220ms
  dropped (shed): 0.4% requests (graceful fallback)
policy B: util_target=85, inflight=72, microbatch_cap=16
  throughput: 128k tokens/s
  p95: 150ms p99: 480ms
  dropped: 2.8% (hard shed during tail spikes)
```
praveen rao: policy A looks safer for SLO. 0.4% shed is acceptable if we have retry/backoff. with B customers will surface timeouts.
alina kozlova: curious about kernel selection path — can we bias kernel chooser to prefer low-latency kernels when near target_util? like runtime hint kernel_preference=latency_over_throughput.
samir patel: we already have a kernel_score that uses predicted batch/seq distribution. adding util-aware bias is doable: score -= alpha*(util - target_util) so when util>target we prefer low-latency kernel. alpha needs tuning.
morgan liu: edge cases: bias could thrash and cause more kernel switches -> cache invalidation -> worse tail. need hysteresis and minimum dwell time for kernel instances.
alex choi: agreed. propose: implement util-bias with hysteresis window 10s and kernel_dwell=30s. run A/B on dedicated pool.
rachel nguyen: also add KV eviction smoothing: if cache eviction rate > 0.5%/s trigger prefetch throttle and temporarily reduce microbatch cap. that should raise hit ratio and reduce tail.
perf-bot: added a checklist: [run A/B on 3 GPUs, collect p95/p99 + kernel switch counts + kv hit_curve, evaluate customer-facing latency].
ops-bot: can deploy canary config to pool: redwood-dedicated-canary-3 at 14:00 UTC.
alina kozlova: one more note — long sequences (>=2048) cause a kernel fallback path heavy on memcpy which amplifies tail. perhaps we should set a per-request seq_limit for high-util pools and route long sequences to a lower-util low-latency pool.
praveen rao: routing long sequences to low-util pool is good. costs more but preserves SLO for interactive traffic. we should add routing rule: if seq>1536 or expected_tokens>512 -> route: low_util_pool.
morgan liu: action items: 1) alex + samir implement util-bias with hysteresis 2) praveen + rachel add routing rule + KV smoothing 3) alina run sim matrix and collect kernel switch metrics 4) perf-bot run 1h canary at 14:00 UTC 5) ops deploy canary.
alina kozlova: will do sim matrix and push results to the thread.
alex choi: thanks team. aim to keep interactive tier p99<250 and try to recover 20% cost from better batching on background routes.
praveen rao: tagging @oncall in case canary needs rollback: @ops-oncall
ops-bot: noted. will monitor and alert if p99>350ms for more than 60s. :rotating_light:
alex choi: ending notes — try to keep messages concise in the canary window. I'll post rollout instructions in #eng-runtime-deploys before 14:00.
